IncidentBot: [P1] 5xx spike on /v1/generate in us-west-2 — error rate 12% (baseline 0.2%). Affected: hosted API customers. Pager sent to #eng-oncall and #support. Incident playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/5xx-generation :rotating_light:

Mike (infra): seeing the alert, looking at edge LB metrics now. Noting TCP resets + backend 502s from runtime pool pool-gpu-12.

Ciara M.: I'm the scheduled secondary for the next 30m, can take handoff if you need to jump. Primary right now?

Mike (infra): I'm primary for this incident. Ciara, thanks — please be ready for handoff at +15m.

Alex R.: quick question — who owns the model-serving 502s vs LB routing? runtime vs infra? I want to avoid duplicate pages.

Sasha (prod-eng): runtime owns model-serving process crashes / OOMs / KV-cache corruption. infra owns LBs, K8s node issues, and network. If 502s are from runtime process returning bad upstream, runtime oncall should be paged.

Mike (infra): current traces indicate connection errors between nginx-proxy and the runtime pods (RSTs). I'm pulling `kubectl logs` for the runtime replica set now.

Support Pager: customer-impact note: multiple customers hitting generation timeouts; Support already opened priority tickets for top 3 accounts. No PII involved.

Mike (infra): pasted checks I'm running:```bash
# sanity
curl -sS https://runtime-usw2.internal/health || true
kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep pool-gpu-12
kubectl logs -n runtime <pod> --tail=200 | grep -i "traceback\|oom\|error" | tail -n 50
```

Ciara M.: I've got a partial runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/handoffs#runtime-vs-infra — suggests we should page `runtime-oncall` if logs show runtime exceptions. If infra-level (node pressure, kernel OOM), page `infra-oncall`.

Alex R.: threshold question — should Security Oncall be involved? Any indicators of malicious traffic or abnormal auth failures?

Security Oncall: at this time not seeing auth anomalies, but if you see unusual client IP ranges or spikes in malformed payloads, escalate to us. For now we can stay in-watch.

Mike (infra): logs show repeated `read: connection reset by peer` and `upstream prematurely closed connection`. Not seeing stack traces or runtime OOM. Node memory fine. Looks like the runtime process is dropping connections under load — paging runtime-oncall. Paging now: @runtime-oncall :rotating_light: 

IncidentBot: Paging runtime-oncall (channel: eng-runtime) — alert forwarded.

Sasha (prod-eng): while we wait, mitigation options: 1) enable fallback routing to model-variant `gen-medium` (less memory pressure), 2) temporarily increase concurrency shed at gateway to protect runtime, 3) scale pool-gpu-12 by +2 replicas for capacity. Which should we try first?

Mike (infra): start with #2 (gateway concurrency throttle) and #1 (failover to gen-medium) simultaneously to reduce pressure. I'll coordinate scaling once runtime confirms health.

Alex R.: runtime-oncall responded in eng-runtime: "Investigating — seeing worker threads crash with EPIPE when proxy drops sockets. Reproducing locally." They recommend applying a quick JVM/worker restart on affected pods.

Ciara M.: note on restarts — do a rolling restart with `maxUnavailable=1` to avoid all pods down. Runbook snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
```

Support Pager: update: Temp mitigation enabled for top-5 affected customers: rate limits increased and retries tuned on the client side. We're notifying them with the standard status template.

Mike (infra): executing gateway throttle: `gatewayctl set-concurrency --route /v1/generate --max 8` — applied. Also initiating scale: `kubectl scale deploy runtime-pool-gpu-12 --replicas=6 -n runtime` (was 4 -> 6).

Sasha (prod-eng): runtime confirmed rolling restart started; monitoring request success rate. Recommend we keep Security Oncall in loop but not page unless we detect exploit indicators.

Security Oncall: acknowledged — standing by. If you need iptables or ACL changes we'll coordinate.

Alex R.: coverage gap note: our overnight rotation currently lacks a second runtime backup between 02:00-05:00 UTC for US-West surge. We should flag for schedule ops — possible additional backup on-call or auto-escalation to infra.

Ciara M.: agree — filing a short post-incident action to add a staggered backup from 01:30-06:00 UTC. I'll create the calendar shift and ping ops.

Mike (infra): success metrics: error rate dropped from 12% -> 1.1% after throttle + rolling restarts + scale. Still monitoring for a stable 0.2% baseline.

IncidentBot: Incident status changed to: Mitigated. Severity: P1 -> P2 for monitoring. Runbook updated: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2163456789-doc

Ciara M.: Handoff summary for next shift (copy to #eng-oncall): Primary: Mike (infra) until 09:00 UTC; Secondary: Ciara M.; Runtime-oncall: Alex R. as responder for runtime issues; Security Oncall: Security Oncall (monitor). Action items: 1) add overnight runtime backup to rota, 2) verify gateway rate-limiter has safe defaults, 3) follow up with runtime team on root-cause fix for socket drops.

Mike (infra): I'm staying on until the morning handoff. If anything flares up, page me directly.

Alex R.: I'll drive the postmortem and own the root cause analysis doc. Will include timeline, logs, and decisions (throttle, restart, scale).

Support Pager: I'll update the affected customer tickets with the mitigation summary and ETA for RCA.

Ciara M.: taking formal handoff at 08:45 UTC (in 15m). Primary now remains Mike until 09:00 UTC. Handoff checklist: runbook link, current mitigations, paging list, and outstanding action items.

Mike (infra): handoff acknowledged. Thanks team. :thumbsup: 

Ciara M.: Handoff complete. I'm now secondary on-call and will escalate to runtime/oncall if we see reoccur. Closing thread as "mitigated — monitoring" in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
